title: Data-center IT power additions by country
unit: MW of IT (critical) capacity added per year, medians
note: Three red-team rounds applied: source audit, colocation-scope audit, forecast-methodology repair (2026-08-13); US 2026E scope correction applied

2022.reasoning: The [German Datacenter Association national database](https://www.germandatacenters.com/fileadmin/images/DCIRD-24/Data-Center-Impact-Report-Deutschland-2024_EN.pdf) places in-scope IT power at 1,202 MW on 1 January 2023. [CBRE recorded 73 MW in Frankfurt in Q4 alone](https://mediaassets.cbre.com/-/media/cbre/countrygermany/data-centre/2022-q4-cbre-europe-data-centres.pdf), so 95 MW is the median national estimate after adding modest Q1-Q3 and secondary-market commissioning; this is an inference, not a reported annual total.

2023.reasoning: The [GDA national study](https://www.germandatacenters.com/fileadmin/images/DCIRD-24/Data-Center-Impact-Report-Deutschland-2024_EN.pdf) reports comparable colocation-plus-hyperscale snapshots of 1,202 MW on 1 January 2023 and 1,349 MW on 1 January 2024, yielding 147 MW. [JLL's 134 MW Frankfurt addition](https://www.jll.com/en-de/insights/german-data-center-market-addressing-rising-demand) corroborates that most, but not all, of the national increase was in Frankfurt.

2024.reasoning: The same-vintage [EUDCA/Pb7 2025 tables](https://www.eudca.org/documents/content/E8VdyUuATTC_BmbNp4nhAwo89?download=0) give 1,330 MW colocation/scale plus 10 MW hyperscale-owned in 2023 and 1,467 + 20 MW in 2024. The corrected addition is (1,467 + 20) - (1,330 + 10) = 147 MW, avoiding the original cross-vintage splice. [Red-team adjusted 2026-08-12.]

2025.reasoning: EUDCA/Pb7's 2026 edition (Table 3 p.72) shows German colocation + scale colocation rising 1,458 to 1,737 MW in 2025 (+279); hyperscaler-owned is flat (Table 4 p.73). Adding JUPITER's 11 MW system load (EuroHPC) gives 290 MW. [Round-3 revision 2026-08-13: pipeline-forecast methodology, KP-verified EUDCA extraction.]

2026.reasoning: EUDCA/Pb7's 2026 edition forecasts German colocation + scale colocation rising 1,737 to 2,167 MW in 2026 (Table 3 p.72), with hyperscaler-owned flat (Table 4 p.73) - a project-level pipeline with delays already discounted. CBRE's 74 MW Frankfurt figure is a metro subset, not a national total. [Round-3 revision 2026-08-13: pipeline-forecast methodology, KP-verified EUDCA extraction.]

2022.reasoning: The [DDA 2023 market study](https://www.dutchdatacenters.nl/wp-content/uploads/lana-downloads/2023/06/SODD-23_Final_140623.pdf) says colocation grew only 1% between April 2022 and April 2023, while hyperscale supplied most of the added MW. [CBRE says Amsterdam's roughly 10 MW in 2022 was one-seventh of its then 2023 forecast](https://mediaassets.cbre.com/-/media/cbre/countrygermany/data-centre/2022-q4-cbre-europe-data-centres.pdf); adding inferred Google/Microsoft self-build phases outside the metro produces a 60 MW national median.

2023.reasoning: [CleanBridge's country series](https://www.cleanbridge.co/insights/energy-transition/cleanbridge-global-data-center-market-report-2025/regional-market-overviews-gdc2025/netherlands-gdc2025/) rises from 1,550 MW in 2022 to 1,638 MW in 2023 for the whole fleet. Because the [DDA reports a declining enterprise segment and strong hyperscale growth](https://www.dutchdatacenters.nl/wp-content/uploads/lana-downloads/2023/06/SODD-23_Final_140623.pdf), nearly all of that 88 MW net increase is assigned to the in-scope fleet and rounded to 90 MW.

2024.reasoning: The same-vintage [EUDCA/Pb7 2025 tables](https://www.eudca.org/documents/content/E8VdyUuATTC_BmbNp4nhAwo89?download=0) give 857 MW colocation/scale plus 460 MW hyperscale-owned in 2023 and 925 + 460 MW in 2024. The corrected addition is (925 + 460) - (857 + 460) = 68 MW; this avoids mixing a DDA observation with a forecast. [Red-team adjusted 2026-08-12.]

2025.reasoning: The [DDA's 2026 update reports 951 MW of colocation at end-2025](https://www.computable.nl/2026/06/09/dda-waarschuwt-ai-golf-legt-zwakte-datacentersector-bloot/), 27 MW above 2024. 2026.reasoning: EUDCA/Pb7 2026 edition: colocation +135 MW (951 to 1,086, Table 3 p.72) plus hyperscaler-owned +35 MW (385 to 420, Table 4 p.73) = 170 MW; the prior edition implies a nearly identical 169, so the forecast is vintage-stable. [Round-3 revision 2026-08-13: pipeline-forecast methodology, KP-verified EUDCA extraction.]

2025.reasoning: The updated [EUDCA/Pb7 national series](https://www.eudca.org/documents/content/ZlZXb4bRSRefaEVqya2I_Aoea?download=0) reports 760 MW at end-2024 and 813 MW at end-2025.
